title: Fiber internet
subtitle: data as light
facts: Fiber-optic internet sends data as rapid pulses (flashes) of light through thin glass strands.
A laser fires light into the strand's core. The core is wrapped in cladding, glass with a slightly lower refractive index, and then a protective plastic coating.
Light hitting the core-cladding boundary at a shallow angle reflects back in (total internal reflection), so it zig-zags along the strand.
Light in glass travels at about two-thirds of its speed in a vacuum: roughly 200,000 km a second. The script never says "the speed of light".
An ocean crossing of about 6,000 km takes roughly 0.03 seconds at that speed, faster than a blink (about 0.1 to 0.4 seconds).

scenes.text: Fiber [internet] sends your data as [flashes] of [light].
A [laser] fires into a glass [core], wrapped in [cladding], then a [coating].
The light [bounces] off the [cladding], [zig-zagging] along the strand.
In [glass], it travels about [200,000] kilometers a [second].
